-Layout (10 points): The layout of the top portion of the page, including the header, timer, and tasks sections, is accurately replicated. -Elements (15 points): Most of the core interactive elements in the top section are present: tabs, timer, buttons, and headings. However, there are several inaccuracies and omissions. The header icons are incorrect; the generated version has a checkmark, and the "login" icon is a person silhouette instead of a dot. A large number of elements from the bottom half of the reference page (two H2 headings, an underline element, and a paragraph) are completely missing. The icon within the "Add Task" button is also different (a circled plus vs. a simple plus). (7/15)
-Content and Text (40 points): All the text in the visible, replicated portion of the page is correct. "Pomofocus," the tab labels, the timer, button text, and task section text are all identical to the reference. The major failure is the complete omission of the substantial text content from the lower half of the reference page, which describes the application. This is a critical loss of content. (20/40)
-Style (15 points): The styling of the generated portion is excellent. The color palette (red background, white text, button colors) is a near-perfect match. The font choices, sizes, and weights for the timer, headings, and buttons are also very accurate. The rounded corners and dashed borders are replicated well. Minor deductions are made for the incorrect icons in the header and "Add Task" button, and for a small, extraneous dot above the "Short Break" tab. (13/15)
-Overall (20 points): The generated page is a high-fidelity copy of the top half of the reference page, successfully capturing the look and feel of the Pomodoro timer application itself. However, it fails completely by omitting the entire informational section below the app. This makes it an incomplete and partial replica. While the replicated part is done well, the missing content is a critical failure. (10/20)

However, the generated page introduces several large components in the middle that are not in the reference. This includes an existing task row, an "Add Task" button, and a "Pomos" status bar. These additions significantly alter the layout and spacing of the central part of the page compared to the reference. (6/10)

Missing elements include the "Time to focus!" text in the header, the small red underline below "What is Pomofocus?", and the grey circle icon in the task editor. The lock icon next to "+ Add Project" has been replaced with a different, incorrect icon. Furthermore, numerous extra elements have been added, such as the entire task list item, the "Add Task" button, and the status bar at the bottom of the task section. (7/15)
-Content and Text (40 points): Most of the text is correct, including the main headings and the labels within the task editor form. However, a key piece of content, the "Time to focus!" text in the header, is missing and has been replaced with "123". The addition of other text elements like the task "123", "Pomos: 0/1", and "Finish At: 14:57" further deviates from the reference image's content. (28/40)
-Style (15 points): The style is the strongest aspect of the replication. The color scheme (red header, white card, grey buttons), font choices (family, size, weight), and general component styling (button shapes, input field appearance) are very close to the reference. The main style deductions are for the missing red underline element and the incorrectly styled icon next to "Add Project". (12/15)
-Overall (20 points): The generated page successfully captures the visual style and branding of the reference. However, it appears to be rendering a different state of the application—one where a task already exists—rather than the initial state shown in the reference. This leads to significant differences in layout, elements, and content, making it a functionally different view, not a direct replication. While the styling is good, the page fails to match the specific view requested in the reference image. (13/20)
